candidates.source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (Hungarian e-procurement platform)
candidates.why_relevant: Mandatory national platform where Hungarian contracting authorities run procedures and publish notices. Structured search by CPV code, subject and place of performance was extended in 2024, so integrator-facing IT/banking-adjacent lots (CPV 72xxx, 48xxx, 66xxx) can be filtered and monitored. This is where 4iG, T-Systems, Delta, NTT Data HU etc. appear as bidders/winners on public-sector IT and payment-related contracts.
candidates.access_status: public web, some functions require registration
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled CPV-filtered search crawls (72000000, 48000000, 66000000 families) + notification/tender-monitoring subscription; parse notice pages for winner, value, framework flag.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on EKR + snowball from procurement guidance sites
queries_used: EKR Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer bank informatikai fejlesztés eljárás keresés

candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság / Közbeszerzési Értesítő (Public Procurement Authority + Gazette)
candidates.why_relevant: Official publisher of Hungarian contract award notices (tájékoztató az eljárás eredményéről) including below-EU-threshold contracts that never reach TED. Primary evidence for which integrator won which public IT / payment-system contract, contract value, and framework agreement structure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic gazette issue crawl + keyword/CPV filter; cross-key winners against integrator actor map.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search; referenced as national portal by OpenTender documentation
queries_used: opentender.eu Hungary tenders.guru Közbeszerzési Értesítő open data award notices

candidates.source_name: DKÜ Közbeszerzési Rendszer – Digitális Kormányzati Ügynökség framework agreement portal
candidates.why_relevant: DKÜ is the centralised buyer for Hungarian government IT under 301/2018 Korm. rendelet. Its keretmegállapodás (framework agreement) portal names the qualified integrator/consultancy suppliers and publishes framework amendments (e.g. KM01ITSZ16 expert services for public-administration IT systems). This is the single best place to see which integrators are pre-qualified to serve state financial bodies (Treasury, tax authority, state-owned banks).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the nyitolap news/asset publisher feed and the framework agreement (KM) register; extract KM identifiers, supplier lists and amendment dates.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on keretmegállapodás + állami informatika
queries_used: keretmegállapodás rendszerintegrátor állami informatika közbeszerzés Magyarország DKÜ

candidates.source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (Hungary filter)
candidates.why_relevant: Above-threshold Hungarian IT/banking procurement notices and award notices in structured, machine-readable form (eForms/XML bulk download). Best baseline for tracking integrator wins with buyer, CPV, value and framework flags, and for CEE cross-border comparison of the same integrators.
candidates.source_subtype: EU official journal supplement / open data
candidates.access_status: public, open API and bulk packages
candidates.suggested_collection_method: TED Search API / daily bulk XML, filter country=HU and CPV 72*/48*/66*, extract winner names and match to integrator actor map.
candidates.discovered_via_method: known EU register, confirmed as upstream of OpenTender Hungary

negative_findings.description: No public, structured 'reference list' of banking-sector engagements was found for the Hungarian arms of NTT Data, DXC Technology or Accenture. English and Hungarian searches surfaced no HU-specific banking case studies for NTT Data HU or DXC HU.
negative_findings.result_summary: Global case-study libraries exist but were not confirmed to contain HU banking references in this pass; HU-entity reference pages were not located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are significant employers in HU financial-services delivery, so their engagements will have to be inferred indirectly (e-beszámoló financials, bank outsourcing registers, job ads, LinkedIn) rather than read off a reference page.

negative_findings.description: No consolidated public register was found that lists private-sector (bank-to-integrator) contract awards in Hungary. Public procurement data covers only public buyers; private bank IT deals appear only via vendor PR, bank outsourcing annexes, or trade press.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for HU bank IT contract registers returned only public-procurement portals and vendor marketing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Roughly half the cell's target universe (commercial bank spend) has no authoritative source; coverage must be assembled from the outsourcing-register and vendor-PR routes, which are incomplete and lagging.

negative_findings.description: Several key Hungarian terms are noisy: 'referencia' also means credit reference/testimonial; 'keretszerződés' vs 'keretmegállapodás' are legally distinct but used loosely; 'pénzforgalom' spans payments traffic and accounting; '4iG' matches unrelated ticker/market chatter.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query results mixed stock-market commentary with contract news for 4iG; consultancy searches returned thought-leadership rather than engagements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Naive keyword collection will produce a high false-positive rate; queries need to be co-constrained with buyer names, CPV codes or document types.

negative_findings.description: For CEE-regional integrators headquartered outside Hungary (Asseco PL, Comarch PL, Sygnity, Ness), no Hungarian-language corpus of banking references was found; their HU-relevant disclosures appear only in Polish or English.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian-language searches returned no HU-market case studies for these vendors.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cross-border integrator activity into Hungary may be systematically under-detected by a HU-language-only collection strategy; Polish and English collection is required for these actors.

negative_findings.description: OpenTender data is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial), and Nemzeti Cégtár/OPTEN detail data is a paid commercial product with scraping restrictions.
negative_findings.result_summary: Licence terms observed on the source pages themselves.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cheapest analytical shortcuts carry licence risk for a commercial intelligence product; primary EKR/TED/Közbeszerzési Értesítő collection should be the backbone, with aggregators used for validation only.

coverage_gaps.description: The HU subsidiaries of global integrators/consultancies (NTT Data Hungary, DXC HU, Accenture HU, IBM HU, Nagarro HU, EPAM HU) were not individually source-mapped in this pass; only their sector context was established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a per-entity pass: company site HU pages, e-beszámoló filings by cégjegyzékszám, HU job postings mentioning bank clients, and LinkedIn company pages, to build one source row per actor.

coverage_gaps.description: Subcontracting calls (alvállalkozói felhívás, beszállítói pályázat) issued by integrators themselves — explicitly named in the cell rationale — were only exemplified (Nádor), not systematically enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Templated path-probing (/kozbeszerzes, /beszallitok, /partnerprogram, /karrier) across every actor domain, plus HU procurement-consultant newsletters that republish such calls.

coverage_gaps.description: State-owned or state-adjacent financial institutions as buyers (Magyar Államkincstár, MNB, Eximbank, MFB, Diákhitel, Takarék/MBH group entities) were not individually checked for their own procurement pages and public-interest data (közadat) publications.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate these buyers, locate each one's közérdekű adatok / közbeszerzési terv page, and add one source row each; their annual procurement plans (közbeszerzési terv) pre-announce upcoming IT tenders.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival/historical source was identified for pre-EKR (before 2018) Hungarian procurement notices, limiting longitudinal analysis of integrator framework positions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test the Közbeszerzési Értesítő historical archive and TED historical bulk packages; if gaps remain, consider web-archive snapshots of kozbeszerzes.hu.

coverage_gaps.description: All URLs in this slice are unverified for liveness; several (t-systems.hu, dorsum.eu, 4ig.hu IR path, kozbeszerzes.hu ertesito path, nisz.hu kozadat path, mnb.hu jelentesek path) were inferred from search snippets or site structure rather than fetched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass; treat any 403/timeout as bot-defence rather than death, and re-resolve 404s from the site's own navigation.

brief: Hungary's integrator layer is unusually legible on the public-buyer side and unusually opaque on the bank side. Public-sector deals are traceable end-to-end through a three-tier stack — EKR and the Közbeszerzési Értesítő for notices, the DKÜ framework portal for who is pre-qualified to sell to the state at all, and TED/OpenTender for structured supplier-level history — with NISZ's HUF 5M+ supplier register and 4iG's BÉT filings giving line-item and revenue-segment corroboration. Commercial bank engagements have no equivalent register: the highest-value substitute discovered is the mandatory outsourcing annex (kiszervezett tevékenységek) that HU banks bury in their ÁSZF document trees, which names actual IT suppliers, backed by vendor reference pages (Dorsum, T-Systems, Asseco CE), the HFA/Infoklaszter member directories for actor discovery, and e-beszámoló filings to size firms whose revenue jumps betray an unannounced win. Hungarian-language search was essential and decisive — the DKÜ framework portal, the NISZ register, the outsourcing annex and the Átlátszó/K-Monitor analytical layer are effectively invisible to English-only queries — while CEE-headquartered integrators (Asseco, Comarch) require Polish/English collection instead.
